images.title: Cost of 4 kg 500 g of rice on a double number line
images.purpose: Show the cost of a weight from the cost of 1 kg: 4 kg cost ₹144, 500 g is half of 1,000 g and costs ₹18, and 4 kg 500 g costs ₹162.
images.composition: A double number line with kg above and rupees below, four matching ticks, one arrow for the part of a kilogram, and the sum below.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. TOP LINE: a thin dark #1F2937 horizontal line at y 270 from x 130 to x 1326 with an open circle (14 px) at each end, and exactly 4 vertical tick marks (40 px tall, 4 px thick) at x 210, 557, 903, 1250, equally spaced (the marks are not drawn to scale). The unit word kg (40 px, bold, teal #0072B2) is at the left end, x 60, above the line. BOTTOM LINE: the same kind of line at y 500 with the same 4 tick marks at the same x positions, directly under the top ticks. The unit word rupees (40 px, bold, amber #E69F00) is at the left end, x 60, below the line. TOP LABELS (centred on the tick, 40 px, bold, dark #1F2937, about y 200): 1 kg at x 210; 4 kg at x 557; 4 kg 500 g at x 903; 5 kg at x 1250. BOTTOM LABELS (centred on the tick, 40 px, bold, dark #1F2937, about y 580): ₹36 at x 210; ₹144 at x 557; ₹162 at x 903; ₹180 at x 1250. ARROW: a dashed teal #0072B2 curved arrow under the bottom line from the bottom tick at x 557 to the bottom tick at x 903, arrowhead at the right end, with the label 500 g costs ₹36 ÷ 2 = ₹18 (36 px, bold, teal) below it at y 670. WORKING TEXT at (383, 150), above the first two ticks (36 px, bold, dark #1F2937): 4 × 36 = ₹144. RESULT at the bottom, y 740: the text 144 + 18 = ₹162 (48 px, bold, teal #0072B2). Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any count of tick marks that differs from 4 on each line
a rupee amount that does not match its weight
a number written with a point or a slash anywhere in the frame
images.takeaway: Whole kilograms cost the number of kg times ₹36; 500 g is half of 1,000 g, so it costs half of ₹36; add them.
images.description: A double number line of kg and rupees: 1 kg ₹36, 4 kg ₹144, 4 kg 500 g ₹162, 5 kg ₹180, with 500 g costing ₹18.
images.context: Concept image for Cost of a Weight. It follows the idea of the double number line in your maths book and uses the concept's own example (practice values: rice at ₹36 for 1 kg).
images.teaching_notes: Read the tick for 4 kg first, then the part. The slip to watch: charging ₹36 for the 500 g.

image_decisions.why: The matching ticks show whole kilograms and the part of a kilogram on one line.
